title: くせに: even though (with blame)
summary: くせに is a contrastive connector like のに, but sharper: it blames someone for acting against what they are.

blocks.text: Two small words say "even though": **のに** and **くせに**. のに is the plain one, so we start there. くせに is its sharper cousin, and it comes second.
**のに** joins two clauses that clash: what you would expect did not happen. It is added to a plain clause, and after a noun or な-noun it becomes **なのに**. The feeling is regret or disappointment.

blocks.jp: 毎日練習したのに、上手にならなかった。
blocks.en: I practiced every day, and yet I didn't get good.

blocks.jp: 休みなのに、会社に行く。
blocks.en: Although it's a day off, (I) go to the office.

blocks.text: のに can also end a sentence, with the second clause unsaid: "if only ...", "and yet ...".

blocks.jp: あんなに頑張ったのに。
blocks.en: And I tried so hard... (it didn't work out)

blocks.text: Now くせに: even though, with blame

**くせに** means "even though / despite", like のに, but with a harsh edge. It takes a person's status or character and says their behavior is the opposite of what you would expect. The 癖 (habit) meaning is not helpful here.
くせ is a noun, so what comes before it modifies it in the usual way.

blocks.jp: お金持ちのくせにケチだ。
知っているくせに教えてくれない。
blocks.en: (You) know it, and yet you won't tell me.

blocks.jp: 男のくせに泣いている。
blocks.en: (He) is a man, and yet he is crying.

blocks.text: The direction can be reversed too: the blame can fall on someone who is bad at something yet keen.

blocks.jp: 下手なくせに威張っている。
blocks.en: (He) is bad at it, and yet he swaggers.
(He) is bad at it, yet keen. (still a criticism)

blocks.text: The second clause is often dropped, as an insult that trails off. Be careful: what follows is a separate sentence, not part of the くせに clause.

blocks.jp: 大人のくせに。泣かないでよ。
blocks.en: And you call yourself an adult. Stop crying.
And you call yourself a man!

items: のに = even though, with regret; くせに = even though, with blame.
Noun の / な-noun な / adjective / verb + くせに.
Usually rude; don't use it with people above you.

questions.note: Like のに, but accusing.
くせに often sounds like severe criticism.

questions.instruction: How does くせ work grammatically in くせに?
options: A noun that follows the modifier
A verb that ends the clause
A particle added to the verb
questions.note: くせ is a noun, so what comes before it modifies it.

questions.prompt: くせに can be used to praise someone.
questions.note: It is nearly always negative.

questions.prompt: The second clause after くせに is sometimes left out.
questions.note: It is implied.

questions.prompt: 学生の＿＿、全然勉強しない。
questions.note: くせに blames someone for acting against what their status suggests.
questions.en: Though (he) is a student, (he) doesn't study at all.

questions.note: A な-noun joins くせに with な.
questions.en: He's healthy, and yet he took the day off.

questions.prompt: 高い＿＿くせに、おいしくない。
questions.note: An い-adjective joins くせに with nothing.
questions.en: It's expensive, and yet it isn't tasty.

questions.note: A noun joins くせに with の.
questions.en: Though (he) is a teacher, he made a mistake.

questions.instruction: Which sentence joins くせに correctly?
options: 知っているのくせに、教えない。
知っているなくせに、教えない。
知っているくせに、教えない。
知っているだくせに、教えない。
questions.note: A verb joins くせに in its plain form with nothing added.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap: you feel regret, not blame
questions.prompt: せっかく準備した＿＿、雨が降った。
questions.note: のに is for regret; くせに would be blaming someone.
questions.en: Although I prepared so carefully, it rained.

questions.prompt: 弟は、何もできないくせに、いばっている。
questions.note: くせに carries blame.
questions.en: My little brother can't do anything, and yet he acts important.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that marks the "despite" clause
questions.note: くせに joins the two clauses with blame.
questions.en: He's bad at singing, and yet he sings.

questions.note: Noun の + くせに: despite being an adult.
questions.en: That person is an adult, and yet cries a lot.

questions.prompt: He is a teacher, and yet he is late.
questions.note: Noun + の + くせに, then the second clause.
questions.en: He is a teacher, and yet he is late.

questions.prompt: You know it, and yet you say nothing.
questions.note: Plain verb + くせに.
questions.en: You know it, and yet you say nothing.

questions.prompt: He is bad at cooking, and yet he cooks every day.
questions.note: な-noun + な + くせに.
questions.en: He is bad at cooking, and yet he cooks every day.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap: regret, not blame
questions.prompt: 朝から待っていた＿＿、彼は来なかった。
questions.note: のに fits plain disappointment; くせに would blame him.
questions.en: I waited since morning, but he didn't come.

options: 親切のくせに、冷たい言い方をする。
親切だくせに、冷たい言い方をする。
親切なくせに、冷たい言い方をする。
親切くせに、冷たい言い方をする。
questions.note: 親切 is a な-word, so it needs な before くせに.

options: You thank a friend for lunch
A famous chef burns the toast and blames others
questions.note: くせに criticizes someone who acts against expectations.

questions.instruction: What does the speaker do here?
questions.note: くせに can trail off as an insult.
questions.en: And you call yourself a teacher!

questions.note: After a noun, のに becomes なのに.
